correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 the three exhaustive overlap types of candidate edges give E[I M] exactly; subtracting known marginals yields the normalized covariance. For n=3 the cubic factor 3p(1-p^2) has one peak above 1. For n>=4 its positive part has strictly decreasing logarithmic derivative, and its exact value at p=1/n exceeds 1; therefore two and only two sign roots occur. The limit of the first root follows from F(c/n)->2c; the second follows from F(t/sqrt(n))/sqrt(n)->t(2-t²)e^{-t²}, t<sqrt(2), together with the positive-domain endpoint. Boundary n=2 has I=M Bernoulli(p). Pure-standard-library verifier exhaustively enumerates n=3,4,5,6 and passes 454 rational/inequality assertions. The all-order proof does not rely on finite checks.

value.rationale: Both counts are natural basic random-graph structural statistics, one capturing isolated connected pieces and the other absence of triangle closure. The exact positive–negative–positive covariance for all n>=3, the sharp n=2 exception, and separated n^-1 versus n^-1/2 roots constitute a global structural dependence classification that cannot be read off from the known marginals and is motivated by sparse-component and triangle-emergence regimes. The exact sparse covariance density is quantitatively useful. No paper-sized extension is claimed.
